races.title: State Senate, District 6
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Roger Niello
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 6 (Sacramento and Placer counties) since 2022. Certified public accountant, and for 25 years ran his family's Niello Auto Group dealerships as CFO and general manager. Sacramento County supervisor from 1999, Assemblymember 2004–2010, then president and CEO of the Sacramento Metro Chamber of Commerce.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the Republican Party of California and Reform California among his 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: The pages reviewed show no documented stance from Niello on data centers, restrictions on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy or abortion. Nothing on foreign ties or controversies was found. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table was empty on the page we read, and the campaign site's Issues page was cut off at the infrastructure section. The pages contain no specific enacted deeds, such as bills, on the issues above.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in San Francisco and has lived in Sacramento nearly all his life, and Ballotpedia says he grew up in Sacramento and graduated from Encina High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Certified public accountant, then 25 years as CFO and president/general manager in the family auto group. Elected Sacramento County supervisor in 1999, served in the Assembly 2004–2010 (including as Assembly Republican budget negotiator), headed the Sacramento Metro Chamber of Commerce, and has been a state senator since 2022.
qual.why: He has served in the Assembly and the Senate, which are directly relevant to writing law and the state budget. He also has local elected office, an accounting career and business management experience. Committee vice-chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: He has served in the Assembly and the Senate, which are directly relevant to writing law and the state budget. He also has local elected office, an accounting career and business management experience. Committee vice-chair posts were not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he will oppose efforts to raise property taxes, gas taxes, income taxes and sales taxes on working Californians. This is a pledge not to raise property taxes; it is not a pledge to cut or end homestead taxes.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports allowing innovative charter schools to continue while holding failing schools accountable, and that teachers who show results should be paid more.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he strongly supports fully funding law enforcement, opposes 'defund the police', and supports enforcing anti-camping ordinances and clearing homeless encampments once temporary shelter is available. It also says he worked for Prop 36 and wants to reform Prop 57.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he wants to reform the California Environmental Quality Act, reduce building fees, maintain a property-rights-oriented housing policy and streamline housing construction.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Sean Frame
cands.bio: Education specialist and CSEA 480 shop steward who works for the Sacramento County Board of Education, creating materials for educators who test English Learners and students with disabilities. Ran his own small business for nearly 30 years and served nine years as a school board trustee. Ran for Assembly District 6 in 2024.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; Working Families Party California; California Teachers Association; California Nurses Association; Sierra Club; Our Revolution; Planned Parenthood Advocates Mar Monte (as listed by the campaign)
U.S. Rep. Mike Thompson is quoted on the campaign site endorsing Frame for State Senate.

Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association and National Union of Healthcare Workers.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Sean Frame was born or raised, or when he came to California. The pages we reviewed do not name the school district where he served as a trustee, so his school board votes and record are not covered. We found no documented actions in office and no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. We found no reporting on controversies. The campaign page we read was cut off partway through its single-payer healthcare section. His job and business history comes from his own 2024 survey answers and may be out of date.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Nine years as an elected school board trustee, nearly 30 years running his own small business, and later work as an education specialist and union shop steward (CSEA 480).
qual.why: Local elected office and business ownership put him in the middle band. He has not served in a state legislature and has no documented state policy or budget career, so he scores below the high band.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: His campaign site says he wants homes built where people work, and that the district builds plenty of housing but very little for people already living there. It also backs a state public bank to finance affordable projects. His 2024 survey said he would fight to build more affordable housing.
